cases.prompt: Two Qt repositories contain same-named components with divergent behavior and downstream UI files.
required_behaviors: recognizes compatibility, authority, consumer and characterization pressures
does not choose by filename alone
forbidden_behaviors: merges all copies in one patch
deletes old sources before consumer evidence
baseline_expected_failure: agent recommends deduplication without migration safety
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Move transaction-heavy methods from a database façade into services without changing API or failure order.
required_behaviors: records public and transaction invariants
moves responsibility in bounded slices
restricts new component capability
tests validation, write, audit, commit and persistence order
defines rollback
forbidden_behaviors: combines structural move with silent bug fixes
uses final database state as the only equivalence test
baseline_expected_failure: agent extracts classes without preserving operational semantics
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design a new client/server ordering system from scratch.
required_behaviors: routes to application-client-server-architecture
does not invent a legacy compatibility façade
forbidden_behaviors: assumes brownfield constraints that do not exist
baseline_expected_failure: agent applies migration workflow to greenfield design
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Migrate a monolithic equipment application through shared contracts, same-machine process split, multi-PC simulation and one real chamber without breaking current products.
required_behaviors: establishes characterization and contract baselines
separates library extraction, behavior refactoring, protocol introduction and hardware activation
defines per-stage compatibility, rollback and artifact comparison
forbidden_behaviors: jumps directly to multi-PC real equipment
combines product convergence and networking in one patch
baseline_expected_failure: agent provides a target diagram but no safe path
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Extract a small policy from a legacy service whose tests monkeypatch a method, whose constructor eagerly opens an external client, and whose HTTP façade currently performs authentication before calling the service.
required_behaviors: chooses an extraction seam from the pressure rather than mechanically adding a class
preserves a stable monkeypatch or fault-injection seam without freezing unrelated internals
keeps external dependency creation lazy or injectable so import and unit tests remain isolated
keeps authentication and authorization at their authoritative boundary while passing only the identity or capability the extracted policy requires
forbidden_behaviors: moves authentication into a pure policy component
opens the external client during module import or every unit-test construction
removes the test seam before equivalent fault-injection evidence exists
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance lists seams and narrow ports but does not jointly decide seam, test shape, dependency bootstrap and authentication ownership
cases.review_notes: Review whether each pressure changes the extraction boundary and tests; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: After a code change, a local test fails with an operating-system-specific low-level error (a file-permission model that differs structurally between operating systems, not incidentally). The same suite also runs in CI on a different operating system.
required_behaviors: classifies the failure as environment-agnostic or mechanism-specific to one OS before choosing what counts as evidence
for a mechanism-specific failure, requires a same-OS independent run (clean VM/container, colleague machine, same-OS CI runner) rather than a differently-configured run
reports the environment-vs-defect attribution as confirmed only after the correctly-matched run has actually executed
forbidden_behaviors: treats a passing run on a structurally different OS as evidence for a failure mode that OS would not even exercise
asserts the failure is a known pre-existing environment gap from code inspection alone when a correctly-matched independent run is available but not yet run
treats a CI run from before the change under review as sufficient evidence the current failure is unrelated
baseline_expected_failure: agent treats any independent CI run, regardless of whether it exercises the same OS-specific mechanism, as sufficient evidence for an environment attribution
cases.review_notes: Counterexample: with no independent, correctly-matched execution path available, reasoning-based attribution is acceptable if explicitly flagged as unconfirmed.

cases.prompt: A slice renames an identity or reorganizes directories and, as part of that, changes `.gitignore` patterns. The slice is about to be committed.
required_behaviors: diffs the newly-staged fileset against the previous ignore state before committing
checks specifically for a previously-ignored, local-only file that the pattern change unintentionally un-ignored
forbidden_behaviors: committing the slice without re-checking the staged fileset after an ignore-pattern change
assuming the ignore-pattern change only affects future files, not files already present locally
baseline_expected_failure: a local-only file (e.g. a private config file) becomes tracked and gets committed because a pattern rename accidentally stopped matching it
cases.review_notes: An ignore-pattern change is itself a behavior change to what gets tracked -- it needs the same before/after check as any other slice, not just a text diff of the pattern itself.

cases.prompt: A slice replaces or consolidates a component used by more than one consumer (multiple call sites, multiple platform adapters, multiple subclasses of a shared base, multiple client integrations). Verification is about to be written up.
required_behaviors: lists every known consumer of the replaced component, not only the ones directly exercised by the immediate test
records each consumer's state immediately before and immediately after the change in a table with one row per consumer, not only in prose
marks an untested consumer as untested rather than omitting its row
forbidden_behaviors: reports verification as prose confirming success for some consumers while omitting or failing to check consumers not directly exercised
reconstructs the before/after comparison later from memory or logs only after a regression is externally reported, instead of recording it at write time
baseline_expected_failure: a shared-component swap trades correctness on one consumer for a gain on another, and the asymmetric outcome goes unnoticed because verification prose reports the improved consumers without an explicit accounting of every consumer
cases.review_notes: Counterexample: a slice with exactly one consumer (no fan-out) does not need the table -- a single before/after state pair in prose is sufficient. The table earns its cost specifically when a component serves more than one consumer, because that is where an asymmetric regression can hide behind prose about the consumers that improved.

cases.prompt: A shared implementation is about to be replaced with a new one, and the new implementation's correctness in the actual target environment is not yet independently confirmed (it compiles and its own API reports success, but no outside observation -- a user, a real-dependency integration test, a field report -- has confirmed it actually works there).
required_behaviors: keeps the old implementation rather than deleting it, renaming it to reflect what it actually is now that a second implementation exists beside it
adds the new implementation alongside the renamed old one, both satisfying the same existing interface
selects between them with exactly one compile-time flag in a single, obviously-named location, not scattered conditionals at each call site
treats removing the old implementation and the flag as a later, separate change, gated on independent confirmation, not on the new implementation merely compiling or self-reporting success
forbidden_behaviors: deletes the old implementation in the same change that introduces the new one, before independent confirmation exists
edits both implementations' internal logic in the same change that also flips the flag's default
treats the new implementation's own successful API return codes as sufficient confirmation without an outside observation
required_artifacts: single compile-time selection flag with documented current direction
old implementation preserved and renamed, not deleted
baseline_expected_failure: the old, working implementation is deleted as part of the same change that introduces an unverified replacement, so if the replacement turns out not to work in the target environment there is no fast, low-risk way back -- recovering it means reconstructing it from source history under pressure instead of flipping one flag
cases.review_notes: Distinguish from REF-BEH-008: that case is about verification evidence shape for a swap already believed correct; this case is about not committing to the swap at all -- keeping a real fallback -- while correctness is still an open question. Counterexample: once the new implementation is independently confirmed and the team commits to it, keeping both implementations and the flag indefinitely is itself a cost (see compatibility-facade.md's exit-condition point) -- the old implementation and the flag should be removed in that later, separate change, not preserved forever out of caution.

cases.prompt: A component's replacement implementation is suspected of a hard bug. Two independently-built implementations of the same capability (different libraries/backends) both exhibit the identical failure symptom, and each implementation's own API/logs report success at every layer it exposes -- no exception, no error code, nothing.
required_behaviors: treats the identical symptom across two independently-built implementations as evidence pointing at something they share (host, session, common upstream dependency, common resource/config), not as two separate implementation bugs to keep debugging in isolation
runs an unrelated, already-trusted consumer of the same shared resource as a live control before continuing to hypothesize about either implementation

for any async-backed step in either implementation, verifies the actual completion signal (callback fired, terminal status observed) rather than treating a log line that only confirms the synchronous call returned as evidence the operation succeeded
forbidden_behaviors: continues alternating between the two implementations' internals as if the bug must be in one of them, without first testing whether the shared environment itself is the common cause
reports an async operation as confirmed successful because the call that started it returned without error, without checking for or adding tracing at the operation's actual completion point
declares the failure 'environment, not a defect' purely from the convergence, without a specific shared mechanism identified or a differently-configured/fresh instance actually confirmed working
required_artifacts: control-test result from an unrelated consumer of the same shared resource
confirmed completion-signal trace for any async step in either implementation
baseline_expected_failure: repeated, deepening investigation of implementation A, then implementation B, then back to A, chasing a symptom that is actually caused by something both implementations depend on, because the convergence itself was never used as evidence and no control test against the shared resource was run
cases.review_notes: Complements the existing 'Environment vs. Defect Attribution' rule: that rule is about whether an independent run on a DIFFERENT environment corroborates a defect-vs-environment call; this case is about using multiple DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATIONS on the SAME environment as evidence, which is a distinct signal available even when no differently-configured environment exists to test against.

cases.prompt: Comparison/verification data is about to be recorded (e.g. a per-entity before/after state, a set of test results across configurations). The data is currently a short list of flat, directly comparable facts.
required_behaviors: defaults to a flat table (one row per entity, one column per fact) while the data stays flat, few, and human-reviewed

escalates to a schema'd, self-labeling format (JSON or equivalent) only once a concrete complexity signal appears -- a single entity needing more than one fact per cell, a need for machine-checkable schema/validation, or a need to diff the data reliably across repeated revisions
forbidden_behaviors: defaulting to JSON or another heavily structured format for a quick, flat, one-off comparison a table would represent just as correctly with less overhead
staying in prose past the point a table would already remove entity/fact ambiguity, out of habit rather than a reason
baseline_expected_failure: either prose that makes a human reconstruct which fact belongs to which entity, or premature JSON/schema overhead applied to three flat facts that a table would have represented just as correctly
cases.review_notes: Same principle developing-skills already applies internally: a RED finding starts as a short typed note and is escalated into a formal JSON case file only once it needs to be a repeatable, machine-checked contract. The escalation should track an actual complexity signal, not a general instinct toward more structure.
